batches.description: Docs (design D2, D4, D5, D7, D9): in docs/04-when-it-stops.md add '### `ARCHIVE PENDING`' under 'The skip receipt' (what it means, that archive is after merge, the exact line) and '### `PUSH FAILED`' under 'The soft continues' (the env vars, that the topic is a secret, INTERLOCK_NTFY_URL for a self-hosted server, that the exit code never changes), and extend 'Reading a SHIP HALTED run' so the run id, project slug and cwd rows are named as the join key and the slug is described as derived from the directory the close ran in; in docs/03-openspec-vs-interlock.md:47 change 'surfaced in `spec` and `mr`' to 'surfaced in `spec`, `mr` and the ship summary'; in docs/10-agentic-workflow-ship-and-spec.md:445 mark the reminder as shipped and non-blocking by design; in README.md change the sentence at :149 to name the one exception (interlock notify and run close --notify, only when INTERLOCK_NTFY_TOPIC is set) and add INTERLOCK_NTFY_TOPIC / INTERLOCK_NTFY_URL to the configuration section; in README.md:54, docs/01-first-hour.md:24 and docs/04-when-it-stops.md:100 replace the enumerated allowlist (interlock, interlock-graph, openspec, git, your test runner) with a pointer to interlock doctor, which prints the derived requiredCommands and the exact rules to add, so the prose never restates the list again; add a CHANGELOG.md entry under Unreleased covering all four wins.

In lib/receipt.mjs (design D4, D5, D7, D8, D9): export summaryHeadline({ change, halted, leftoverTaskIds }) returning the exact first line and use it inside formatRunSummary; extend formatRunSummary's destructured options with runId = undefined, root = undefined, projectSlug = undefined, push = null, unarchived = null, all defaulted. After the 'commit:' row and the notes loop, push '  run: <runId>' or '  run: none — the run halted before a plan was adopted' when runId is not a non-empty string, then '  project: <projectSlug>' and '  cwd: <root>' when provided; then '  push: sent (ntfy)' or '  push: failed — <reason>' when push is an object with sent defined. Immediately before 'Do not start another ship run unless the user asks.', when !summary.halted && leftover.length === 0 && unarchived && unarchived.thisChange, push 'ARCHIVE PENDING — <change>: after merge, run openspec archive <change>' and, when unarchived.others > 0, '  also unarchived: <n> completed change(s) — run interlock drift'. Keep every existing line byte-identical. In test/workflows.test.mjs beside the direct formatRunSummary call at :2289, add direct-call assertions: defaults print 'run: none — …' and no archive line; a clean run with unarchived: { thisChange: true, others: 2 } prints both archive lines; a halted run with the same input prints neither; leftovers print neither; push: { sent: false, reason: 'HTTP 403' } prints the failed row; none of the new lines contain 'LEAN SHIP' or 'No degradation banners'.

Create lib/project-slug.mjs exporting projectSlug(absPath) = every character outside [A-Za-z0-9] replaced by '-' (design D9), with a header comment citing the observed ~/.claude/projects rule and the four observed mappings ('/', '.', space, '_'). Create test/spine/project-slug.test.mjs asserting /Users/x/IdeaProjects/specflow -> -Users-x-IdeaProjects-specflow and /Users/x/Application Support/repo/.claude/worktrees/w_1 -> -Users-x-Application-Support-repo--claude-worktrees-w-1, and that a non-string input throws.

In lib/limits.mjs add notifyTimeoutMs: 5000 to LIMITS with a doc comment (a hanging relay must not stall the close; design D5), and print it in formatLimits as 'push timeout (ms)'. In test/spine/limits.test.mjs pin the value; the existing reader sweep at :159 is satisfied by the non-test reader task 1.1 provides in lib/notify.mjs.

Verify — do not edit — that .claude/settings.json is tracked (git ls-files --error-unmatch .claude/settings.json exits 0) and that its permissions.allow contains all nine rules: the six present today plus "Bash(test:*)", "Bash(printenv:*)" and "Bash(mkdir:*)". The human adds the three rules and stages the file at the checkpoint, because it is a host-protected settings file an in-run agent must not touch (design D11). If either check fails, halt with a result naming the exact three lines to add and the 'git add .claude/settings.json' command; do not write the file yourself.

In lib/doctor.mjs (design D5, D12): append { tokens: ['test'], open: true, why: 'the environment probe checks for the graph and the test profile (workflows/ship.js)' }, { tokens: ['printenv'], why: 'the environment probe reads CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL and the Bedrock variables' } and { tokens: ['mkdir'], why: 'the environment probe creates .claude/ship/' } to REQUIRED_COMMANDS; export HOST_READ_ONLY (frozen array ls cat echo pwd head tail grep find wc which diff stat du cd) with a comment naming the Claude Code permissions page and the date checked (2026-09-07); add checkNotify(env) returning check('notify', 'ok', 'push configured: <server url>') when INTERLOCK_NTFY_TOPIC is set (never the topic) or check('notify', 'skip', 'INTERLOCK_NTFY_TOPIC is not set — optional; an unattended run that stops will not reach you'), wired into diagnose outside run() with its own try/catch that yields skip. Update test/spine/doctor.test.mjs: the required-count assertion at :234-254, the uncovered list and fix text at :256-274 (now also test, printenv, mkdir and their Bash(<name>:*) suggestions), a notify ok/skip/never-value test, and HOST_READ_ONLY contains echo and pwd and not test/printenv/mkdir. Add the repo-fact test: read <repo>/.claude/settings.json, parse allow rules with parseRule, and assert every entry of REQUIRED_COMMANDS plus this repository's own runner commands 'npm test' and 'node --test' (pinned explicitly because .claude/testing/profile.json is gitignored and absent on CI) has a covering rule via ruleCovers, adding profileCommands(profile) only when the profile file exists; never call diagnose on the repo. Export extractInstructedCommands(text) from lib/doctor.mjs: every 'Run:' / 'Then run:' line, and every backticked span whose first token matches /^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$/ and that also contains a space, a '-' flag or a '/' path; split on &&, ||, ;, |; return each subcommand's first token after stripping quotes, '$(' and VAR=value prefixes; skip spans listed in an exported, pinned IGNORED_INSTRUCTION_SPANS. Unit-test the extractor against synthetic strings — one instructing 'chmod +x bin/x' must yield chmod, one with 'echo $PPID' must yield echo, one with 'test -f a && echo yes || echo no' must yield test and echo. Then the live drift test: run the extractor over workflows/ship.js and every lib/prompts/*.mjs and assert every command is in REQUIRED_COMMANDS ∪ {npm test, node --test} ∪ HOST_READ_ONLY, failing with file and command.

Create lib/notify.mjs (design D1, D2, D4, D5): export NOTIFY_TOPIC_ENV = 'INTERLOCK_NTFY_TOPIC', NOTIFY_URL_ENV = 'INTERLOCK_NTFY_URL', DEFAULT_NTFY_URL = 'https://ntfy.sh'; readNotifyConfig(env) returning { topic, url }, { topic: null } when unset, or { invalid: '<VAR>' } when the topic contains whitespace or '/' or the URL does not parse (never echo the value); composeCloseMessage({ headline, change, runId }) -> { title: headline, body: 'change: <name>\nrun: <runId>' or 'run: none — the run halted before a plan was adopted', priority: headline starts with 'SHIP HALTED' ? 'high' : 'default' }; composeCheckpointMessage(change) -> title 'SPEC CHECKPOINT — <change>' at default priority; postNtfy({ url, topic, title, body, priority }, { fetchImpl = globalThis.fetch, timeoutMs = LIMITS.notifyTimeoutMs }) -> { sent: true } or { sent: false, reason } with reasons 'HTTP <status>', 'network error: <message>', 'timed out after <ms>ms', 'invalid configuration: <VAR>', every reason passed through sanitizeReason(reason, { topic, url }) that strips the topic and server URL, collapses newlines and caps at 200 characters; use AbortController; POST to <url>/<topic> with Title and Priority headers. Create test/spine/notify.test.mjs with an injected fetchImpl covering success, 403, network error, timeout, unset topic, invalid topic, default URL and a self-hosted URL, asserting no reason string contains the topic or the URL including for an injected error whose message contains both.

In lib/run.mjs (design D1, D5, D7, D8, D9, D14): import detectUnarchived from ./drift.mjs, projectSlug from ./project-slug.mjs, readNotifyConfig, composeCloseMessage, postNtfy from ./notify.mjs, and summaryHeadline from ./receipt.mjs; make runClose async and accept notify = false. After degradationLines and before buildReceipt: compute absRoot = resolve(root) and slug = projectSlug(absRoot); compute unarchived inside a try/catch mirroring readLeftoverIds: { thisChange: detectUnarchived(root).some(u => u.change === manifest.change), others: <count of the rest> }, and on any throw set unarchived = null and push 'archive check skipped: <reason>' onto manifest.notes so a clean close never exits 1 over an unreadable sibling change; when notify is true, read the config — unset topic -> push = null; invalid -> push = { sent: false, reason: 'invalid configuration: <VAR>' }; otherwise await postNtfy(composeCloseMessage({ headline: summaryHeadline({ change: manifest.change, halted: haltReason, leftoverTaskIds }), change: manifest.change, runId: manifest.runId }), …) — and on sent === false push 'PUSH FAILED: <reason>' onto degradations. Pass runId: manifest.runId, root: absRoot, projectSlug: slug, push, unarchived to formatRunSummary; leave exitCode computed exactly as today. On the no-manifest early return, also attempt the push when requested (headline 'SHIP HALTED — <reason>', runId null) and append '  run: none — the run halted before a plan was adopted', '  project: <slug>', '  cwd: <absRoot>' and the push: row to that summary text. Extend the close tests in test/spine/run.test.mjs: a clean close prints run: <runId>, project:, cwd: and ARCHIVE PENDING — <change> and exits 0; a fixture second change with all boxes ticked yields 'also unarchived: 1 completed change(s)'; a fixture sibling change whose tasks.md is unreadable (a directory in its place) still closes with exit 0, no ARCHIVE PENDING line, and an 'archive check skipped:' note; a --halt close prints no ARCHIVE PENDING; a close without --notify and with INTERLOCK_NTFY_TOPIC set in the child env prints no push: row and makes no request; a close with --notify against a loopback http.createServer stub (INTERLOCK_NTFY_URL=http://127.0.0.1:<port>) records one POST to /<topic> with Title equal to the summary's first line and Priority: high on a halt, and prints 'push: sent (ntfy)'; a 403 stub yields 'push: failed — HTTP 403', a 'PUSH FAILED: HTTP 403' banner, no 'No degradation banners' line, and the same exit code as without --notify; the topic value appears nowhere in the summary or the trajectory file.

In bin/interlock (design D1, D14): add notify to BOOLEAN_FLAGS; in the run dispatch pass notify: flags.notify === true and await runClose; make main an async function and replace the try { main() } catch at the entry point with main().catch(err => { … same body … }); add case 'notify': 'interlock notify --title <t> [--body <b>] [--priority high|default]' and the sugar 'interlock notify checkpoint <change>' (uses composeCheckpointMessage), printing 'push: not configured — set INTERLOCK_NTFY_TOPIC' and exiting 0 when unset, 'push: sent (ntfy)' and exit 0 on success, 'push: failed — <reason>' and exit 1 on failure; add the usage/help row and the --json shape { sent, reason }. In test/spine/cli.test.mjs add: notify with no topic exits 0 and says not configured; 'notify checkpoint add-thing' against a loopback stub posts title 'SPEC CHECKPOINT — add-thing'; a 500 stub exits 1 with the reason.
In workflows/ship.js and bin/interlock-run, append '--notify' to the array each closeArgs() returns (design D1); nothing else changes in either driver — no env read, no topic, no notification text.

In skills/spec/SKILL.md §6 (design D6 — delete this task if the ledger answer is ship-only), add one step immediately before the 'GOAL MET: interlock spec stopped at the checkpoint.' line: run 'interlock notify checkpoint "<name>"', noting it is a no-op that exits 0 when no topic is configured. In test/skills.test.mjs beside the checkpoint test at :428, assert the spec skill contains the token 'interlock notify checkpoint' and that it appears before the GOAL MET line.

In test/workflows.test.mjs (design D1, D5, D7, D12): extend the verbatim-strings test at :1101-1117 so lib/receipt.mjs contains 'ARCHIVE PENDING — ', 'also unarchived: ', 'run: none — the run halted before a plan was adopted' and 'push: sent (ntfy)', and workflows/ship.js contains none of them; extend the banner-party test at :111-133 so lib/run.mjs raises 'PUSH FAILED: ' and workflows/ship.js does not; add a network-isolation test asserting that among lib/**/*.mjs, bin/* and workflows/*.js only lib/notify.mjs contains 'fetch(' or 'globalThis.fetch', and that neither driver contains 'ntfy' or 'INTERLOCK_NTFY'; extend the driver-parity test at :1319 (or add beside it) so both drivers' closeArgs() source contains '--notify'; add a cross-surface test that lib/drift.mjs, lib/receipt.mjs and skills/mr/SKILL.md all contain the token 'openspec archive '; assert README.md names 'interlock notify' in the sentence that claims the CLI runs without the network, and docs/04-when-it-stops.md contains headings for ARCHIVE PENDING and PUSH FAILED.

Run 'openspec validate harden-unattended-ship-runs --strict', 'interlock validate harden-unattended-ship-runs', 'interlock ledger harden-unattended-ship-runs' (D6 remains needs_human until answered — record that in the handoff rather than resolving it), 'npm test', 'npm run validate', and 'interlock doctor' (expect notify: skip when the topic is unset and permissions: ok with nine required commands on this repository).

1.7.summary: Docs updated per D2/D4/D5/D7/D9: docs/04 gained ### ARCHIVE PENDING (under skip receipt) and ### PUSH FAILED (under soft continues), plus the SHIP HALTED section now names run/project/cwd rows as the trajectory join key with slug derivation; docs/04:100 and docs/01:26 and README:54 now point at `interlock doctor` instead of enumerating the allowlist; docs/03:47 names the ship summary as a third drift surface; docs/10 item 3 (line ~445) is marked shipped and explicitly non-blocking by design; README:149 names the notify/run-close network exception and a new '### Configuration: push notifications' section documents INTERLOCK_NTFY_TOPIC/INTERLOCK_NTFY_URL; CHANGELOG.md Unreleased/Added gained one entry covering all four wins (push, identity rows, archive reminder, doctor hardening).
1.7.next: Wave 2 (lib/run.mjs, bin/interlock, drivers) and task 3.1's verbatim/cross-surface tests can rely on these doc anchors (#archive-pending, #push-failed, #configuration-push-notifications) existing.

1.4.summary: Added exported summaryHeadline({change,halted,leftoverTaskIds}) to lib/receipt.mjs and used it for formatRunSummary's first line; extended formatRunSummary with defaulted runId/root/projectSlug/push/unarchived; after the commit row and notes loop it now always prints a `  run:` row (real id or the 'none — the run halted...' fallback), then `  project:`/`  cwd:` when provided, then a `  push:` row when push is an object with `sent` defined; immediately before 'Do not start another ship run...' it prints `ARCHIVE PENDING — <change>: after merge, run openspec archive <change>` (plus `  also unarchived: <n> completed change(s) — run interlock drift` when others>0) only when !summary.halted && no leftovers && unarchived.thisChange. All prior lines are byte-identical (verified via existing 154 workflows.test.mjs cases plus the new one). Added one new direct-call test 'identity rows, the push row and the archive reminder (design D7, D8, D9)' in test/workflows.test.mjs (next to the :2289 formatRunSummary call) covering: defaults print the 'run: none —' fallback and no archive line/project/cwd/push rows; unarchived:{thisChange:true,others:2} on a clean run prints both archive lines; the same input on a halted run and on a run with leftovers prints neither; push:{sent:false,reason:'HTTP 403'} prints the failed row; none of the new rows contain 'LEAN SHIP' or 'No degradation banners'.
1.4.next: npm test: 1756 pass, 1 pre-existing unrelated failure in test/spine/limits.test.mjs (LIMITS.notifyTimeoutMs has no reader yet — that's task 1.1's postNtfy, not part of 1.4 and present before this task started, confirmed via git stash). test/workflows.test.mjs (154 tests) and node --check on both changed files pass clean. Task 2.1 still needs to wire lib/run.mjs to actually pass runId/root/projectSlug/push/unarchived into this formatRunSummary call.

1.2.summary: Created lib/project-slug.mjs exporting projectSlug(absPath) replacing every non-alphanumeric char with '-', with header comment on the four observed mappings; added test/spine/project-slug.test.mjs covering both example paths and non-string throw.
1.2.next: Task 1.3 (limits.mjs notifyTimeoutMs) or others in wave 1 can proceed independently.

1.3.summary: Added LIMITS.notifyTimeoutMs=5000 with doc comment, formatLimits row 'push timeout (ms)', and a pinning test in test/spine/limits.test.mjs. New test passes. The pre-existing reader-authority sweep test now fails naming LIMITS.notifyTimeoutMs as unread, exactly as the task text warns ('requires the non-test reader that 1.1 provides') — lib/notify.mjs (task 1.1) does not exist yet.
1.3.next: Task 1.1 must create lib/notify.mjs referencing LIMITS.notifyTimeoutMs so the cap-authority sweep test passes again.
1.3.blocker: Reader-authority sweep test in test/spine/limits.test.mjs fails until task 1.1 (lib/notify.mjs) lands, as anticipated by the task description's own dependency note.
